title: Check yourself: where patterns go, and where uncaught exceptions go

questions.stem: Per this page, where can Java 21 pattern matching be used to inspect a caught exception?

options.text: In the catch clause's header, as a type pattern with a guard
options.says: The page says the catch clause itself has no pattern syntax.

options.text: Inside the catch block's body, through instanceof but not switch
options.says: The page says switch patterns can be used there since Java 21, alongside instanceof since Java 16.

options.text: Inside the catch block's body, through instanceof or switch
options.says: The page names instanceof and switch patterns used inside a catch block, and says the clause itself takes none.

questions.stem: Per this page, what happens to an exception thrown in a try block that no catch block anywhere matches?

options.text: It moves up the call stack and ends the program with a trace
options.says: The page says it propagates up the call stack and, caught nowhere, terminates the program and prints a stack trace.

options.text: It is dropped there, and execution carries on after the try statement
options.says: The page says an unmatched exception propagates; nothing drops it.

options.text: It is turned into an Error, and the thread waits for a handler
options.says: The page describes propagation up the call stack, not conversion or waiting.
